question: Should the ConvLSTM classify the U-Net's ROI crop (the geometry the architecture diagram shows) or the whole slice?
decided_on: validation macro-F1 only; neither run loaded the test split
split: dataset Training/Testing split; validation carved from Training only; image-level split; no patient identifiers
notes: Both runs used the same split, the same seed and the same default hyper-parameters; they differ only in the input geometry.

The ROI run was given 120 epochs with patience 15 and early-stopped at 103, so it was trained to convergence rather than cut off by the epoch cap. An earlier 40-epoch run reached 0.9439 and was still improving, which is why it was repeated.

Why the crop loses: the segmentation it depends on scores Dice 0.656, so a crop often cuts into or misses the lesion, and the context outside the box — which the whole-slice model can still use — is discarded.
The ROI checkpoint is kept at weights/method1/baseline_classifier.pth as evidence. It is not served and was never evaluated on the test set.
